findings.summary: README's figures on the test's data overstate the fp8 floor: at N = 128 and on causal rows it covers 27-73% of elements, not 81-100%, and Post accepts 0 on 89.5-100%, not 97.7-100%
findings.detail: Lines 207-212 and 405-408 say that on the test's data Post accepts o = 0 on 97.7% to 100% of the sampled elements, and that p's fp8 rounding alone (sum p|v| / (8 sum p), about 0.05) is at least |attnRef| on 81% to 100% of them, so 'on the test's data that is the fp8 rounding of p itself'. Over every test_op shape (work/tol.out, Model.lean's formulas; at N = 128 every row of the head), Post accepts 0 on 89.5% (D = 64, N = 128, causal) to 100%. The fp8 floor is at least |attnRef| on 38-49% (D = 64) and 27-39% (D = 128) of the elements at N = 128, and on 54-73% of the causal rows at N = 1024 and 4096. It reaches 80-100% only on the non-causal rows at N >= 1024. So on the test's N = 128 shape and on causal rows, the reason Post does not reject 0 is mostly Num.DotE5m2's pE (L124), not the fp8 rounding. The README's opening (line 12, 'part of that is the fp8 rounding itself; the rest comes from Num.DotE5m2') is right. To resolve: give the ranges over every test_op shape, and say that the fp8 floor explains the non-causal rows at N >= 1024, while the rest (N = 128, causal rows) is L124's part.
findings.evidence: work/tol.py, work/tol.out: the lines '0 accepted: ... by Post (tolO and tolV) on ...' and 'fp8-rounding floor ... >= |attnRef| on ...' for D = 64 and 128, N = 128, 1024, 4096, both values of causal.

release.note: Settled. Post now also bounds o by tolV, which is computed over the kernel's own p, so pE does not enter. I re-ran work/tol.py on the new formulas. On the benchmark's data at N = 1024, tolV has median 6.6 (D = 64) and 6.8 (D = 128), against tolO's 1.2e4 at D = 128, and it agrees with my round-1 magnitude estimate within 1.08x. On a one-key causal row tolV is 0.308 |attnRef|, so Post rejects 0 there. The README's figures for tolV agree with mine: 2.9 / 7.1 (test), 144-145 and 358 at N = 2^14, the v = 1 row, and kappa 0.53 at 2 blocks, 0.22 at 16, none from 32 (none already at 31). The rest is stated as a limitation with L124, which is the route F4 offered. Rejecting 0 on the test's and the benchmark's data would need a sharper library fact.

Settled. kernel.json's title, the README's opening ('Read this first') and its kernel paragraph, and the root docstring now say that only the first ceil(Z*H/HEAD_DIM) heads read v and the others output ±0. 'Meaningful on the test's shapes and data' is gone. The table gives the benchmark's D = 128 (tolO 1.2e4, tolV 6.7) and N = 2^14.

notes: On the other reviewer's findings (not mine to release): F1's resolution (b), a plainly stated limitation, is now in the README's Specification and Narrowings. With tolV added, I see nothing left for the kernel to do on F1, apart from the figures in my new DOC finding. F2 is rightly a library matter (L124). F3 is done in the four places the response lists. The new spec's constants print as TVA, Mathlib or kernel definitions (work/print_spec.lean, print_spec.out). main, consistent and satisfiable still use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Mag.lean has no instance, notation or option other than maxHeartbeats. The decision my round-1 notes raised still stands for the coordinator and the user: whether a certificate is wanted for a kernel whose Post records that most of the host's heads output ±0.
